hints.title: Subsequence Bitmask Representation
hints.text: Because string length is at most twelve, each subsequence corresponds to a non-zero bitmask up to two to the power of twelve.

hints.title: Precompute Palindromic Masks
hints.text: For every mask, construct the chosen characters and verify if the formed string reads identically forward and backward.

hints.title: Disjoint Bitwise Condition
hints.text: Two subsequences are disjoint if and only if their bitmasks share no bits, meaning mask one bitwise and mask two equals zero.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.time: O(2^N * N + P^2) where N is string length and P is the number of palindromic bitmasks
complexity.space: O(2^N) to store valid palindromic bitmasks and lengths
complexity.notes: Small constraints allow full enumeration of subsets and pair testing.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursively partitioning characters without bitmasks creates redundant recursive tree branching.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Precomputing palindromic bitmasks avoids repeating palindrome checks across disjoint pairs.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should leverage small input bounds by modeling subsequences as bitmasks.
